research_question: Among adults with chronic kidney disease not requiring dialysis, what is the effect of statin therapy (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors) versus placebo or no statin treatment, with co-interventions given equally to both arms, on end-of-treatment urinary protein excretion?
treatment_label: Statin therapy (e.g., pravastatin, atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, fluvastatin, lovastatin, cerivastatin, or simvastatin) in adults with non-dialysis chronic kidney disease
control_label: Placebo or no statin treatment, with all other treatments applied equally between arms
outcome_description: Proteinuria at the end of the randomized treatment period, measured as 24-hour urinary protein excretion or, only when it is the study's sole measure of urinary protein loss, 24-hour urinary albumin excretion. Extract the final end-of-treatment mean, SD, and analyzed participant count for each eligible arm. Use the last on-treatment assessment before any washout, crossover, or withdrawal phase; do not use baseline or change-from-baseline values. Standardize values to g/24 h (including mg/24 h or mg/day divided by 1000), while recording original units and conversions. Convert SE/SEM to SD using SD = SE × square root of n after checking table footnotes and methods; eligible figure-only data may be digitized, with error bars interpreted and converted appropriately. For duplicate or companion reports, retain one trial-level dataset from the report containing the full randomized sample. In multi-arm studies, include only eligible CKD statin and placebo/no-statin arms. Do not analyze kidney function, lipids, cardiovascular events, mortality, adverse events, or urinary podocytes.
positive_direction: For directionally harmonized standardized effects, a positive Hedges g would mean less end-of-treatment proteinuria with statin therapy than with placebo or no statin and therefore favor statin; for the user-specified raw mean difference in g/24 h, however, a negative MD means less proteinuria and favors statin.
search_queries: statin chronic kidney disease proteinuria randomized trial
HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor urinary protein excretion placebo controlled
pravastatin atorvastatin rosuvastatin simvastatin CKD albuminuria trial
inclusion_criteria: Original empirical comparative studies of adults with chronic kidney disease not requiring dialysis that evaluate a statin against placebo or no statin, with other treatments provided equally across eligible arms.

Studies reporting end-of-treatment 24-hour urinary protein excretion, or 24-hour urinary albumin excretion when it is the only urinary protein-loss measure, with quantitative information potentially usable to calculate an effect size.
Any eligible statin, CKD cause, treatment duration, publication status, language, or setting, including multi-arm studies when the relevant CKD statin and placebo/no-statin arms can be isolated.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, and theoretical papers.

No comparison between an eligible statin treatment and a placebo or no-statin control condition; this includes statin-versus-statin and statin-versus-other-active-drug comparisons without an eligible control.

No quantitative end-of-treatment outcome data capable of producing an effect size (e.g., arm means with SD/SE, suitable t/F statistics, proportions, or odds ratios), after reasonable derivation or figure extraction.

Completely unrelated to the research topic, or involving only dialysis recipients, kidney-transplant recipients, non-CKD participants, ineligible urinary outcomes, or outcomes other than proteinuria/albuminuria without separately extractable eligible CKD data.
moderators_to_extract: Underlying CKD etiology and clinical population (e.g., diabetic versus non-diabetic CKD)
Treatment duration and timing of the final on-treatment assessment
Concomitant renin-angiotensin-system blockade or other equally applied kidney-protective therapy
effect_size_note: Pool the raw mean difference (statin minus control) in end-of-treatment urinary protein excretion, expressed in g/24 h, using a random-effects model. Thus MD < 0 indicates lower proteinuria and favors statin. Use final values only, not baseline values or change scores. Prefer 24-hour total urinary protein; use 24-hour urinary albumin only if it is the study's sole urinary protein-loss measure. Convert mg/24 h or mg/day to g/24 h by dividing by 1000 and document original units and conversion. Convert arm-level SE/SEM to SD as SD = SE × sqrt(n), after verifying whether reported ± values or figure error bars are SD or SEM. Digitize eligible final means and error bars from figures if necessary. Use the last on-treatment timepoint before washout, crossover, or withdrawal. Avoid double-counting multiple reports by linking reports at the trial level and extracting once from the report with the full randomized sample. For multi-arm trials, include only eligible CKD statin and placebo/no-statin arms and handle any shared control without double-counting if more than one eligible statin arm is retained. Assess heterogeneity with tau-squared and I-squared, report the pooled MD with 95% CI and prediction interval when estimable, inspect influence/outliers, and conduct sensitivity analyses for albumin-versus-total-protein measurement, figure-derived data, and high risk of bias. Assess risk of bias using an appropriate randomized-trial tool where applicable and assess small-study effects with funnel plots and regression tests only when enough studies are available.
